{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-24, going one level under his own redb question: *"a more fundamental question after this line of thinking, but what does having a db (whether that be rocksdb or redb or other) give us versus just using the reflow2 json file as what endures? does having a db allow us to do things we wouldn't otherwise have?"* Nothing here is intent and nothing is planned.

⭐⭐ THE QUESTION IS UPSTREAM OF BOTH EARLIER ONES, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS SEPARATE. `dec:idea-a-byte-backend-that-compiles-in-seconds` asks WHICH engine. `dec:idea-the-store-becomes-a-session-cache-and-the-export-becomes-the-truth` asks WHAT IS DURABLE and still assumes a per-session store. This asks whether an embedded key-value store earns its place AT ALL. All three can be answered independently and the answer to this one changes whether the other two matter.

⭐⭐ MEASURED 2026-08-24, AND THE BUILD HAS ALREADY ANSWERED THE LOUDEST HALF. `crates/reflow2-core/Cargo.toml` declares **`default = []`** — `rocksdb` and `fulltext` are BOTH optional and BOTH off by default; only `reflow2-mcp` turns them on (`features = ["rocksdb", "fulltext"]`). Consequence, measured by running it: **`cargo test -p reflow2-core --no-default-features` passes 1,452 tests with NO database and NO search index**, against 1,760 for the whole workspace with both features on and the MCP surface included. ⇒ **The design-graph operations do not depend on a byte store.** Schema validation, the golden thread, adjacency traversal, the detectors, HEAL, propagation, the graph algorithms — all of it runs on `MemoryBackend` (`foundation/store/backend.rs:245`), which is the same `KvBackend` trait with a `BTreeMap` behind it.

WHAT A STORE ACTUALLY BUYS, then — a short list, and it is shorter than it looks:
1. **DURABILITY WITHOUT A WHOLE-DOCUMENT REWRITE.** One changed node writes one key, not 8.4 MB. This is the real one and it is the ONLY one that is hard to replicate.
2. **CRASH CONSISTENCY.** RocksDB's WAL means a killed process loses the last write, not the file. A half-written JSON document is corrupt — recoverable only by write-to-temp-and-rename, which is atomic but gives all-or-nothing at whatever cadence you write.
3. **LARGER THAN RAM.** Irrelevant at reflow2's own size: 3,142 nodes = 8.4 MB export, and it is the biggest design anybody has.

WHAT PEOPLE ASSUME IT BUYS AND IT DOES NOT — the part worth writing down:
- **Query power.** reflow2 asks graph questions — neighbours, traversals, type scans. Those come from `graph_id`-namespaced keys and an adjacency index (`keys::adj_out_key`), and `MemoryBackend` serves them by the same code path. There is no query planner and no SQL to lose.
- **SEARCH.** `fulltext` is its OWN feature, tantivy, independent of the KV store. `search_design` needs an INDEX, not a database, and an index is derived — rebuildable on hydrate from the document.
- **MULTI-SESSION CONCURRENCY.** That is the shared SERVER (a process holding one writer), not the store. Sessions share a graph because they share a process, and that stays true whatever the bytes sit on.

⇒ THE SHAPE THE ANSWER SEEMS TO TAKE, offered as a finding and not a conclusion: for one person on one laptop, an embedded store buys **durability and crash-safety and nothing else**, and the alternative is not redb — it is `MemoryBackend` plus the document at boundaries, which reflow2 ALREADY SUPPORTS FOR EVERYTHING EXCEPT PERSISTENCE. Every graph operation is proven on it by 1,452 passing tests.

⚠️ THE COST OF BEING WRONG, recorded beside the idea rather than used to argue it down. The trade is **bounded loss vs no loss.** RocksDB's durability is real engineering and hard to reproduce honestly; write-temp-and-rename gives atomicity but loses everything since the last write. Anyone taking this road is choosing a weaker durability story deliberately, and `dec:idea-what-guarantees-the-export-if-the-export-is-the-only-durable-copy` is where that half is argued.

🛑 WHAT IS UNMEASURED AND DECIDES IT: hydrate time. Parsing 8.4 MB of JSON, building the adjacency index and building the tantivy index, to first query. Nobody has taken it. Today's 2.4-second figure is an EXISTING store opening with its index already on disk — the cheap half, and not this number.

📌 THE OVER-ENGINEERING READING, in his own terms. What RocksDB currently costs this project, measured: a ~19-minute librocksdb-sys C++ compile on every clean build, the bulk of a target directory that reached 263 GiB, a pin on the historically-unmaintained `rocksdb` 0.24 with a migration to `rust-rocksdb` still owed, and 86 files of absorbed store code now in reflow2's tree to maintain. That is the price of durability for an 8 MB document. Whether it is worth paying is exactly the question he asked, and it has never been asked in that form before.","name":"OPEN — what does ANY embedded store buy over the export document alone? Measured: 1,452 of the core's tests already pass with no database and no index, because `default = []`","rationale":"Captured under the brainstorm skill: recorded as an idea, nothing promoted, nothing settled.

This asks whether an embedded key-value store earns its place at all — and unlike the other two it is already half-answered by the build, since `default = []` means 1,452 core tests run without one today.","status":"proposed"}
